nodes.title: About this pass
widgets_values:
### Base pass
Whole frame at 768x960. Rig colour proxy as init, openpose, depth and lineart controls.

**Denoise 0.7:** run gk-style-20261104c (0.56 washed out faces).

**IP-Adapter:** two adapters, `style transfer` at 0.6, square head and outfit crops, rig attention masks. A/B in art_runs/studio-proof-20261104/ipadapter: `linear` copies the reference's teeth and thick mustache; `style and composition` grows a beard on `left_hand.peak` and is refused by test_studio.

Control strengths are the `moderate` profile; `extra.kumbia.variants` writes `peak`, `overlap` and `turn` API files from this same source.

nodes.title: About this pass
widgets_values:
### Shirt pass
The mask's interior is wiped with the rig proxy, then sampled at 0.35 (cheat sheet's starting value, kept by test). At 0.5 the stripes break into dots on the 8px cells; without the wipe, 0.35 can't remove the base's speckle.

The composite keeps every pixel outside the mask identical.

nodes.title: About this pass
widgets_values:
### Embroidery pass
A prompt alone doesn't make embroidery: at 0.55 it stays plain stripes and differs per frame. So one strip cut from the reference is laid along each rig stripe (stage_parts.py), then sampled lightly with tile control at 0.3 to sit it into the shirt. The stitches are the same in every pose because they start as the same pixels.

Embroidery can't survive 96x120: see the size sheets in art_runs/studio-proof-20261104.

nodes.title: About this pass
widgets_values:
### Head pass
`$head_xy` is a blank image whose width and height are the window's x and y (stage_parts.py): core nodes can't read a box from a mask, and only images bind per pose.

The base face is **wiped** with `$face`, a face drawn from the rig's mustache, before sampling. Without this, 0.5 denoise keeps the base's teeth and thick mustache, and 0.8 from flat skin loses the face on a tilted head.

**Denoise 0.55 by test:** art_runs/studio-proof-20261104. Pixel LoRA made little visible difference between 0, 0.35 and 0.8 here.

The paste uses a tighter mask than the sampler, so the seam sits on freshly sampled pixels.

nodes.title: Read me
widgets_values:
# Frame multi-pass
base > shirt > embroidery > hat > head > matte. Each pass has its own save node.

Edit anything here and Save, then `sync_studio.py pull` brings it back to the repo. Change the pose by picking other files in the `$` Load Image nodes: titles starting `$` bind at run time, so keep them.

`colourmatch.py` and `studio.finish_pixels` run after this graph, outside it.

Guide: tool/art/studio/README.md
